title: Ranked students
hints: Check `len(names) != len(scores)` first. Then build the index slice: `idx := make([]int, len(names))` and `for i := range idx { idx[i] = i }`. Put this in a small helper both functions can call.

Sort the **indices**: `slices.SortFunc(idx, func(a, b int) int { return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(scores[b], scores[a]), strings.Compare(names[a], names[b])) })`. Note `b, a` for the descending score. `names[idx[0]]` is now the winner.

For competition ranking, walk `for pos, i := range idx`: when `pos == 0` or `scores[i]` differs from `scores[idx[pos-1]]`, set `rank = pos + 1`; otherwise keep the previous rank. Then `fmt.Sprintf("%d. %s (%d)", rank, names[i], scores[i])`.
